findings.problem: The interjection lane still has no agent-facing surface. Measured call sites on the settled revision: appendMailboxDeduped -> tools.js:1876/:1895 (wired); expireInterjections -> scheduler.js:300 (wired); enqueueInterjection -> NONE; decideInterjection -> NONE (the only non-definition hit in lib/ is the JSDoc line scheduler.js:231); clearMailboxToWatermark -> NONE; readLiveMailbox -> NONE. So no agent can ask for an interjection, the captain cannot approve or reject one, and no surface can clear a mailbox: the frozen R1 intent (a member must be able to ASK the captain) and the frozen clear-authority rule (captain may clear any mailbox, a member only its own) are still unimplemented at the tool boundary. The t49 completion payload and evidence/omo-align/messaging/r1-wiring/result.json claim the opposite ('R1 is now consumed at the tool boundary; no R1 criterion rests on an unreferenced export'), while the same directory's dead-capability-findings.md documents the truth.
findings.requiredFix: Decide and implement the tool surface (which tool exposes enqueueInterjection / decideInterjection / clearMailboxToWatermark and to whom each is authorized) - a design decision to escalate to the user, not a mechanical repair. Also correct/supersede the t49 record so a later reader cannot conclude the lane is reachable.

findings.problem: The TTL is bound to idle edges, not to wall-clock: the expiry tick lives at the top of kickMember (scheduler.js:293-307), so a team that never kicks again after a request leaves the row pending past its TTL indefinitely and the requester is never told, while the shipped wording ('TTL 30 minutes', 'onCaptainSilence') reads as wall-clock. This matches the accepted fix text ('call expireInterjections on the scheduler's idle edge'), so it is a boundary rather than a defect.
findings.requiredFix: State the boundary explicitly in the contract/ledger (expiry is evaluated at idle edges, not by a timer), or also tick once at session start so a dormant team still resolves past-due requests.
